newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia bonds bounce as US extends gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia bonds bounce as US extends gains.

text.p: *Australian bonds bounce in SYCOM on stronger Treasuries,
*U.S. FOMC holds U.S. rates steady, focus now on local rate change at 9.30 a.m. announcement time and U.S. payrolls later.
*NAB Quarterly business survey due this morning

Australian bonds turned around Wednesday's losses in overnight trading, pulled higher by a second successive stronger close in U.S. Treasuries, and are expected to remain buoyed in case of a local rate cut today.
Treasuries rose on a decision by the U.S. FOMC to leave U.S. rates unchanged at 5.50 percent, and on short-covering and hedge fund buying ahead of the June payrolls report on Thursday.
Both the local three and 10-year September futures contracts pushed through resistance levels they had failed to hold in Wednesday's fall, with the 10-year yield moving back below 7.00 percent.
Although the 10-year futures ended SYCOM above the 93.020 level, they may be under some pressure ahead of the payrolls data and against a lessening odds of an imminent local rate cut.

"The lack of U.S. topside potential into tonight and a still hesitant short end makes the outright potential on the day down, back to the 92.940/950 support," Westpac technical analyst Peter Pontikas said.
While rate cut hopes have been wound back, the FOMC outcome meant the front end should be well bid ahead of the 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time for any cut by the RBA.
